blindSummary:
Trans visitors face serious risk in this country despite the absence of criminalisation. The most acute documented traveler-axis risk is the police: in February 2024 the interior ministry began investigating officers who beat, tortured and sexually harassed two LGBT people during a raid on an apartment in the capital. About 105 sexual-orientation/gender-identity-motivated incidents were recorded in 2024, a masked attacker smashed the front of the LGBT community's pride information centre in 2025, pride marches require heavy police protection, and testosterone HRT supply-chain disruptions have been documented.

The country sits outside its region's visa-free travel area (so border checks apply to foreign travellers), legal-gender-recognition reform has stalled (a gender-identity law was not adopted), and the anti-discrimination law is weakly enforced - public institutions are described as making "minimal effort". One mitigating factor is a capital prison's trans-sensitive search policy, which lets trans women choose the search arrangement, though watchdogs flag training gaps.

The country has had an openly lesbian head of government, but stalled legislation and police brutality make that largely symbolic rather than substantive protection. The capital, the main tourist hub, is "conditionally" manageable with situational awareness.
blindOutOfScope: General crime and border corruption affect all travellers; the country is not part of its region's visa-free area, so border checks apply to foreigners.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional investigative-journalism network (Feb 2024): this country is investigating allegations of police assault on two LGBT people during a drugs raid on an apartment in the capital - the interior ministry's internal-control unit referred the complaint, filed by a rights-monitoring NGO, to the prosecutor's office.

Rights-monitoring NGO (Sept 2025): presentation of its 8th annual report on transphobia and homophobia in this country - 105 incidents motivated by homophobia and transphobia in 2024, the highest number since monitoring began; includes quantitative and qualitative analyses of hate speech, hate crimes and discrimination.

International torture-prevention organisation's country page: national preventive-mechanism overview (the national human-rights ombudsman body, operational since 2011, cooperating with six civil-society organisations) and links to the country report on detention safeguards.

International human-rights organisation world report 2025, chapter covering this country and a neighbouring territory: intolerance and violence against LGBT people remained significant concerns in 2024, alongside attacks on journalists and a flawed asylum system (section on sexual orientation and gender identity).

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: trans people face testosterone supply shortages (a branded testosterone preparation); a publication analysed 70 instances of politicians' hate speech (April 2023-April 2024); the pride information centre was attacked in January and announced closure in September after 20+ attacks since 2018, none properly sanctioned; a survey poll found three-quarters of trans/non-binary people fear job interviews due to anticipated discrimination.

National trans organisation's guide for foreigners: practical guide to living and transitioning here - rights, medical access, hormone supply; discrimination based on trans identity is prohibited by law but not always abided; transphobic attacks in public spaces are rarely physical but prejudices are common; recommends avoiding prominent LGBTIQ symbols, large sports events (hooligan risk) and trusting one's instincts.

A foreign government's 2018 human-rights report on this country: human-rights issues include government corruption, violence against journalists, and 'crimes including violence targeting lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex (LGBTI) individuals'.

International LGBT-rights organisation: this country's anti-discrimination law adopted - a 2009 statute explicitly prohibiting discrimination on sexual-orientation and gender-identity grounds, a regional milestone.
blindLocalsOnly: The stalled gender-identity law and the weakly enforced anti-discrimination law are resident-facing; the capital prison search policy concerns resident detainees; the HRT supply disruptions affect residents.
